name: Chon-Kyzyl-Suu Gorge
near: Kyzyl-Suu (formerly Pokrovka), the district centre, ~30 km west of Karakol; from the village ~25 km up the gorge to the geophysical station.
elev: Valley floor in the lower part ~2,000 m; Jyluu-Suu hot springs 2,340 m; hut 2,500–2,550 m; geophysical station 2,600 m (Destination Jeti-Oguz, Nomad's Land); ridge up to 4,500 m, Kyzyl-Suu peak.
short: Chon-Kyzyl-Suu is a gorge south of Kyzyl-Suu with red cliffs in the lower part, the hot sulphur springs of Jyluu-Suu (43–45 °C), an old geophysical station-hut at 2,600 m and routes to lakes and glaciers.
desc: The Chon-Kyzyl-Suu gorge (“big red water”) begins at the district centre Kyzyl-Suu and over 25 km climbs from ~1,800 to 2,600 m. The river got its name from the muddy red colour of the water eroding red sandstones. 15–20 km from the village are the Jyluu-Suu hot sulphur springs (43–45 °C) in simple concrete baths, and another 4 km on is the old geophysical station of the Tian Shan Observatory, which works as a hut (a room with 4 beds, a Kyrgyz floor room, a Russian banya (sauna), camping, horses, guides) at the fork of the Karabatkak and Ashuu-Tor gorges. Higher up are Lake Savator (Salvator), the Ashuu-Tor waterfalls, the Shatyly cascade (100 m) and Sharkyratma (20 m), the Karabatkak glacier with its lake, and Kyzyl-Suu peak. The Archa-Tor, Savator and Teleti passes link the valley with Jeti-Oguz and the Karakol gorge; routes also lead on to Altyn-Arashan. Snow leopard, bear, ibex and marmots live here. The road is paved at the village, then dirt with fords, a 4x4 or a local driver is needed; the season is May — October.
guide: Drive into the gorge from Kyzyl-Suu without hurrying: the first kilometres are red cliffs, from which the river got its “red” name, then spruce and sea buckthorn. After 15–20 km by the river are the concrete Jyluu-Suu baths with 43–45 °C water: a Soviet bathhouse without gloss, but almost without people; sometimes there is no one even to take the fee. Another 4 km and you are at the geophysical station: here you can spend the night at 2,600 m, steam in a Russian banya and in the morning go to Lake Savator or the waterfall in Ashuu-Tor; arrange horses with the hosts. If you plan a trek to Jeti-Oguz via Archa-Tor — set out from here, it is 2–3 days. From below, drive only in a 4×4 or with a local driver: after rain the fords rise, and there is no phone coverage above the village.
see: The Jyluu-Suu hot springs (43–45 °C, sulphur); the geophysical station-hut at 2,600 m; Lake Savator; the waterfall in the Ashuu-Tor gorge, the Shatyly cascade (100 m) and Sharkyratma (20 m); the Karabatkak glacier with its lake; the red cliffs of the lower part; sea buckthorn and barberry at 2,000 m; birds wintering by the warm springs.
skip: You have no 4×4 or budget for a driver — it is 15–25 km uphill on foot from the village. You want well-appointed thermal baths — here are Soviet-style concrete tubs. You are choosing between this gorge and Jeti-Oguz with one day — Jeti-Oguz is more accessible and more spectacular for a short visit.
diff: The drive to the springs and station — moderate (dirt, fords, 4x4); walks near the station — easy; trips to Savator, the waterfalls and the glacier — moderate (one-day side trips with 300–700 m of gain); crossings of the Archa-Tor/Teleti passes — hard (3,500–3,800 m, 2–3 days).
when: May — October (saigatours: in winter the road is closed by snow); July — September for treks to the glacier and passes; the springs are pleasant in the cold months too, if the road is passable.
hours: An open area, around the clock (Google Maps: “Daily: 24 hours”). The springs have no fixed hours, the attendant is not always there; the hut at the station — by arrangement/booking (Nomad's Land, Destination Jeti-Oguz).
daytime: Leave Kyzyl-Suu in the morning (fords are lower, and you can return by daylight); soak in the springs in the evening after a trek; the red cliffs of the lower part look best in low sun.
how: From Karakol 30 km west to Kyzyl-Suu (marshrutka (minibus)/taxi), then south up the gorge: the asphalt quickly gives way to dirt, ~15–20 km to the Jyluu-Suu springs and ~25 km to the geophysical station (4x4 or a local driver). On foot/by bicycle along the road is an option for the prepared. Hiking entries: from Jeti-Oguz over the Archa-Tor pass, from the Karakol gorge over Teleti.
needcar: Yes: to Kyzyl-Suu — marshrutka/taxi; up the gorge — a 4×4 or a local driver; above the station — on foot or by horse.
self: Yes, with a 4×4 or on foot/by bicycle; no permits; an overnight at the hut by arrangement or in a tent. For the passes experience and a map are needed; no phone coverage.
roadtype: Paved in Kyzyl-Suu, then a dirt road along the river with bridges and fords (issykkul.biz), for a 4x4 or high clearance; above the station — trails.
traveltime: Karakol — Kyzyl-Suu 30 km, ~40 min; Kyzyl-Suu — springs 15–20 km, ~1 h; — station 25 km, 1.5–2 h (Nomad's Land: the whole way from Karakol 58 km, ~3 h 15 min with stops). Side trips from the station: to Savator and the waterfalls — 3–6 h; over Archa-Tor to Jeti-Oguz — 2–3 days.
stay: The hut at the geophysical station (2,500–2,600 m): a room with 4 beds, a Kyrgyz floor room, a Russian banya, camping, meals at a local family (Destination Jeti-Oguz, Nomad's Land; price not published). At the springs — a guesthouse with national cuisine (Nomad's Land). Guesthouses in Kyzyl-Suu “from $4–7 per person” (issykkul.biz, undated). The Ak-Tash yurt camp in the upper reaches (Wanderlog, not confirmed).
net: Kyzyl-Suu has coverage; higher up the gorge, at the springs and the station — no phone coverage (general reports; operators not checked separately).
entry: Free in the gorge. The Jyluu-Suu hot springs — a symbolic fee of “less than $5” (up to ~400 som), sometimes there is no one to accept payment (saigatours, 2024–2025). The exact 2026 tariff in som is not confirmed.
transfer: Carriers’ prices are not published; Nomad's Land and Destination Jeti-Oguz — on request. A guide from neighbouring routes: a 4×4 with a driver from Karakol for the day 5,000 som (Tosor/Jeti-Oguz/Barskoon, 2024).
bring: Swimwear and a towel for the springs, warm layers (nights at 2,600 m are cold), a rain jacket, boots for fords and trails, cash (hut, springs, horses), food for the day, an offline map/GPS, a torch, a first-aid kit; for trekking — a tent and sleeping bag.
warn: The road has fords — after rain and during snowmelt the river rises and a passenger car cannot pass. No phone coverage above the village. Sulphur springs of 43–45 °C — do not sit longer than 15–20 min, do not bathe after alcohol. In the upper reaches — wild animals (bear), herders’ dogs. In 2022 a SaryTours article described the location differently — follow the Destination Jeti-Oguz description via Kyzyl-Suu.
food: National dishes at the guesthouse by the springs and at the family at the station (beshbarmak, lagman, kumys in summer); sea buckthorn and barberry in the lower part (in season); in Kyzyl-Suu — a bazaar with local produce and cafes.
reviews: Google Maps (“Chon-Kyzyl-Suu gorge”, a point near Ayu-Tor/Jyluu-Suu): 4.9/5, 27 ratings as of 03.10.2026. TripAdvisor/2GIS: no separate listing for the gorge found. From 2024–2025 blogs: pros — wild hot springs with almost no people, a hut with a banya, a beautiful road; cons — a hard access road, primitive baths, no phone coverage.
p.sum: From Karakol — a marshrutka to Kyzyl-Suu (≈40 som, 30 km), then a local taxi up the gorge: the first 10 km ≈200 som, the next 10 km ≈400 som (Against the Compass), or your own 4×4. 15 km from the village are the hot concrete baths of Jyluu-Suu (43–45 °C, up to $5); from them ≈5 km on foot (1.5 h) to the geophysical (weather) station at 2,580 m: a hut for 18 with no electricity or running water, a banya, horses, guides. Stay overnight at the Ak-Tash yurt camp (12 places, three meals a day and a banya) or at the station. In the morning — a side trip to the Karabatkak glacier and lake (14 km, +700 m, 6 h). A horse crossing to Jeti-Oguz over the Ak-Sai pass (2,805 m) — 21 km in 6 h, on foot over Archa-Tor (3,900 m) — 3–4 days.

p.iti.2.title: Combinations

p.season: May–June: the road opens, fords are full. July–September: treks to glaciers and passes, yurts operating. October: golden, cold, the springs are especially pleasant. November–April: the road is snowed in, Ak-Tash is a ski-touring base (with a guide).
p.budget.economy: ≈2,000–3,500 som per person per day: marshrutka 40, local taxi 200–600 per car, springs up to 400, a tent or a guesthouse in Kyzyl-Suu $19.
p.budget.comfort: ≈6,000–10,000 som per person: a 4×4 with a driver ≈5,000 som/day, Ak-Tash with meals and a banya, a guide and horses, a Nomad's Land tour.
p.permits: Not required. The gorge is free; the springs have a symbolic fee (up to $5).
p.access: For children — the springs and Ak-Tash (50% discount under 10). For older people — by car to the springs. By stroller — no. With a dog — yes, but there are herders’ dogs and wild animals.
